ops.title: FP bridge socket: App Group container + TCC consent mechanics
ops.body:
Why the File Provider data socket (pool.FPBridgeSocketPath) and the daemon's FP bridge serve loop are shaped the way they are.

## Socket location
- The daemon binds the socket; the sandboxed FP extension dials it for computed content. It MUST live in the App Group container (~/Library/Group Containers/<AppGroupID>/) — the one location BOTH sides may touch: the sandboxed appex gets blanket container access, and the daemon is an entitled group member.
- Sandbox file temp-exceptions do NOT cover AF_UNIX connect — connect(2) is a network-outbound operation, so a socket parked anywhere else is unreachable from the appex no matter what file exceptions it holds.
- The leaf is deliberately short ("b.sock") to keep the full path under the 104-byte sun_path limit.

## TCC consent gating (startFPBridge / serveFPBridge)
- macOS gates the group container behind a TCC consent keyed to the daemon binary's cdhash, so the FIRST bind after every install or upgrade can park on a prompt launchd never surfaces to the user.
- The container MkdirAll therefore runs INSIDE the retried serve loop (serveFPBridge), never on startFPBridge's caller path: it can hang on the pending prompt, or fail while consent is denied, and retrying picks up a late approval.
- serveFPBridge, unlike the holder content bridge, retries abnormal exits with a capped backoff: every FP domain's computed content depends on this one bridge, so transient failures (restart races, a stale peer mid-teardown, the TCC-parked MkdirAll) must self-heal rather than wait out a daemon restart. ctx cancellation cuts the backoff sleep short so wg.Wait never blocks on a sleeping retry.
- startFPBridge waits only a bounded fpBridgeWait for the socket to accept (so an FP Setup's first enumeration finds the bridge up). If it doesn't come up while the daemon is alive AND no hard bind error was recorded, that is the consent-pending signature: flagged on fpConsentPending for status/doctor, and a watchdog clears it the moment the socket lands.
- os.ErrPermission from the bind path is the TCC denied/parked signature (stays eligible for consent-pending); any other error is a genuine bind failure that must not be reported to the user as a consent prompt (fpBridgeHardErr).

## Shared source
startFPBridge is the sibling of startContentBridge, sharing the SAME PoolContentSource instance: the Source contract requires concurrency safety, and the write-through mutex is package-level, so write-throughs serialize across both bridge servers in the one daemon process.
ops.when: working on the daemon's File Provider bridge (startFPBridge/serveFPBridge), FPBridgeSocketPath, app-group-container consent failures, or 'bridge socket not accepting' diagnoses
